summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for a flare of chronic pancreatitis, presenting with epigastric pain radiating to the back, nausea, and vomiting. She was treated with IV fluids, hydromorphone, ketorolac, and anti-nausea medications, with gradual advancement to a soft diet. Her pain and nausea improved, and she was transitioned back to oral medications. New concerns included dental caries, particularly in tooth #8, prompting a referral to oral surgery for planned extractions with antibiotic prophylaxis. Anticoagulation with lovenox was stopped after completing treatment for a prior line-associated DVT. Blood pressure was managed with continued amlodipine and addition of lisinopril. She was discharged home with home health services, instructions for Hickman line care with ethanol locks, and follow-up plans for dental and primary care.
